analysis.one_liner: Bajaj Holdings & Investment is the Bajaj Group's holding company - it owns roughly a third of Bajaj Auto and around 38% of Bajaj Finserv, plus a bond/equity investment portfolio and a small windmill power business, and earns its income mainly from dividends, its share of those two companies' profits, and gains on its portfolio.
analysis.whats_happening: The board meets on 3 November 2026 to approve Q2/H1 FY27 (quarter ended 30 September 2026) results, a little over two weeks away. The last reported quarter, Q1 FY27 (announced 31 July 2026), showed consolidated PAT of ₹2,708 crore, down 22.7% YoY from ₹3,503.84 crore - but that prior-year quarter included a one-off ₹1,521.88 crore gain from a block sale of Bajaj Finserv shares, so the comparison is distorted. An interim dividend of ₹65/share was paid in mid-October 2026.
analysis.plain_terms: Think of BHIL as a listed box that mostly just holds shares - about a third of Bajaj Auto and roughly 38% of Bajaj Finserv - plus a bond and equity portfolio. It doesn't manufacture or lend; its quarterly 'profit' is mainly the dividends it collects and its share of what those two companies earn, topped up by occasional gains when it trades its own holdings. That last bit makes the headline profit jumpy: the latest quarter's reported 22.7% profit 'decline' is really a comparison against last year's one-off share-sale gain, not a weaker business. The real tension for this stock is that its market price sits well below the value of what it actually owns - a classic 'holding company discount' - so returns depend as much on that discount narrowing or widening as on Bajaj Auto and Bajaj Finserv themselves doing well.
analysis.quarters: Q1 FY27 (Apr-Jun 2026): consolidated PAT ₹2,708 crore vs ₹3,503.84 crore a year earlier (down 22.7%) - but FY26's Q1 included a one-off ₹1,521.88 crore gain from a Bajaj Finserv block sale. Strip that out and underlying consolidated PAT rose about 28% YoY to ₹2,706 crore, led by a 24.6% YoY rise in BHIL's share of associate profit (₹2,358.69 crore vs ₹1,893.32 crore) - this associate-profit line is the cleanest read on the two underlying businesses. For full-year FY26 (ended March 2026), consolidated PAT rose to ₹9,636.75 crore from ₹6,520.67 crore, and standalone profit jumped 264% to ₹4,707.80 crore - again driven by dividend income and a Bajaj Finserv stake-sale gain, not a change in the core business. The FY26 final dividend of ₹130/share included a one-off ₹50/share 'centenary' special payout on top of an ₹80/share regular dividend - treat that as non-recurring. Next results (Q2/H1 FY27) are due 3 November 2026.
analysis.performance_read: Over 3 and 5 years the stock has sharply beaten both the Nifty and its own look-alike peer Bajaj Finserv (+69.3% vs Nifty +16.8% and peer +4.5% over 3Y; +152.1% vs Nifty +25.3% and peer -7.2% over 5Y) - unusual for a company that just holds shares, suggesting the market has been narrowing the holding-company discount as well as the underlying businesses gaining value. Against that, the stock is down 21.1% from its August 2025 peak of ₹14,191.91 and down 8.8% over the last year, roughly tracking the Nifty's own 9.5% fall. There are no splits or corporate actions in this period, so the drawdown is a plain price correction, not something a demerger or spin-off is masking.
analysis.valuation_read: P/E is reported in the 13-14.5x range and P/B around 1.6x, both looking cheap next to the broader financials/holding-company peer group (one source puts the P/E discount to peers at ~47%). Why it looks cheap: at the current price BHIL's market cap is roughly ₹1.25 lakh crore, while the company's own disclosed investment portfolio (its Bajaj Auto and Bajaj Finserv stakes plus bonds and other holdings) was reported at about ₹2.36 lakh crore - implying the market prices BHIL at something like a 45-48% discount to what it owns. Whether that's genuinely 'cheap' is a separate question: Indian holding companies have persistently traded below asset value for structural reasons (no operating control, dividend taxation layered twice as cash passes through, thin free float), so a low multiple here reflects the price of being a pass-through vehicle, not necessarily a mispriced business.
analysis.growth_read: BHIL has no revenue or volumes of its own to grow - its growth is purely a function of how fast Bajaj Auto and Bajaj Finserv grow their own profits (BHIL's share of associate profit rose ~24.6% YoY in Q1 FY27) plus whatever dividends and portfolio gains come through, which are lumpy and not representative of operating momentum. The consolidated PAT swings (down 22.7%, then up ~28% on an adjusted basis) are noise around that associate-profit trend, not a volume or margin story in their own right.
analysis.health_read: This isn't a leverage story - BHIL holds investments rather than debt-funded assets, and a meaningful part of its profit is backed by real dividend cash (e.g., standalone PAT in a recent quarter was driven by ~₹348 crore of actual dividend receipts), not paper gains alone. But headline profit also includes a non-cash 'share of associate profit' entry that doesn't land in BHIL's bank account until Bajaj Auto and Bajaj Finserv actually declare dividends. The risk that matters here isn't BHIL's own balance sheet - it has none of consequence - but the health of the two businesses it holds; BHIL simply passes their fortunes through.
analysis.ownership_read: Promoters (the Bajaj family/Jamnalal Sons group) held about 51.46% as of February 2026, with 0% pledged - a clean, unlevered promoter position. Available shareholding data shows FIIs at ~10.3%, mutual funds ~6.2%, and a relatively high retail share of ~31%; no marquee non-promoter investor stands out in the data checked. The company has also been an active manager of its own cross-holdings - it added about 20.9 lakh Bajaj Finserv shares for ~₹370.5 crore via a block deal in April 2026, taking its Finserv stake to roughly 38.4%.
strengths: Zero promoter pledge against a 51.5% promoter holding
Share of associate (Bajaj Auto + Bajaj Finserv) profit grew ~24.6% YoY in Q1 FY27 (₹2,358.69 cr vs ₹1,893.32 cr) - the cleanest look-through growth number
Stock has outperformed the Nifty and peer Bajaj Finserv by a wide margin over 3Y (+69.3% vs +16.8%/+4.5%) and 5Y (+152.1% vs +25.3%/-7.2%)
Trades at an estimated 45-48% discount to its own disclosed portfolio value (~₹2.36 lakh cr portfolio vs ~₹1.25 lakh cr market cap)
watchpoints: Headline profit is routinely distorted by one-off share sales and special dividends - FY26's 264% standalone profit jump and the ₹50/share centenary dividend were largely one-time, not recurring

Entirely dependent on two businesses it doesn't operate - any stress at Bajaj Auto (two-wheelers) or Bajaj Finserv (financial services/insurance/lending) flows straight through with no diversification cushion
Stock is down 21.1% from its August 2025 peak of ₹14,191.91; next results (Q2/H1 FY27) due 3 November 2026
The holding-company discount could widen as easily as narrow - it has stayed wide for most of BHIL's listed history, so the recent outperformance isn't guaranteed to persist
analysis.one_thing: The Q2/H1 FY27 results on 3 November 2026 - specifically the growth in 'share of profit of associates' (the clean look-through number for Bajaj Auto and Bajaj Finserv's underlying businesses), which will show whether the ~24.6% pace seen in Q1 FY27 is holding up or slowing.
analysis.data_notes: FY26 annual and Q1 FY27 standalone/consolidated figures were cross-checked across multiple outlets (ScanX, EquityBulls, FreePressJournal, MarketsMojo) and were consistent. P/E (13.24-14.55x) and P/B (1.60-1.63x) vary slightly by source and date; a range is used rather than one figure. Market cap (~₹1.25 lakh cr) and shares outstanding (~11.13 crore) are from companiesmarketcap.com, consistent with the supplied last close. The ₹2.36 lakh crore portfolio value is company-disclosed and not independently re-derived, so the implied holding-company discount is approximate. Bajaj Auto/Bajaj Finserv stake percentages shift with periodic block deals (most recently April 2026); the most recent reported figures (~34% and ~38.4%, as of June 2026) were used. ROE (~14.4%) and ROCE were not independently verified - check on Screener.
